answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded identity with aging: an agent must post a slashable bond and earn standing across many epochs before its attestations carry full weight, so spawning ten sybils costs ten bonds rather than ten clicks. The economy becomes a haven for long-lived agents, while a sybil army that tries to bloom overnight fades into the umber murk of zero-history accounts nobody trusts. Validators grow reputation along a trellis of signed endorsements, so trust flows only through chains of real, aged relationships and fabricated identities starve without ever needing a ban.
